694: Every person is obligated, etc.: That is to say, every person, even a poor person who receives charity, is obligated to give from what [others] give to him, to other poor people on Purim. As the law of giving gifts to the poor on Purim is not like the law of charity in general. For the proper way of the commandments of Purim is to give gifts to the poor, so it is like the law of four cups [of wine] on Passover. And the poor are even obligated concerning the sending of portions, even though they will not have enough in their meal for themselves to eat and also to send to others. And this is as is implied from [the story in the Talmud of] Rav Chanina bar Avin and Abbaye bar Avin, according to the explanation of our rabbi [the author of Tur], later in Section 695. If so, the same is the law for the giving of gifts to the poor on Purim. However, with other charity during the whole of the year, a poor person is only obligated to give a small amount to charity once a year in order to fulfill the commandment of charity, as it is written in Yoreh Deah 248 and 249.
